question.text: A listed company wants to make a preferential issue. The relevant date is April 1, 2025. Per the current NISM IX workbook, the 90 trading days VWAP of the related equity shares preceding the relevant date is Rs. 150, and the 10 trading days VWAP is Rs. 170. For frequently traded shares, what is the minimum issue price?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the current NISM IX workbook, the preferential-issue floor for frequently traded equity shares listed for at least 90 trading days is the higher of (i) the 90 trading days VWAP and (ii) the 10 trading days VWAP, both preceding the relevant date. Higher of Rs. 150 and Rs. 170 is Rs. 170, so the minimum issue price is Rs. 170. The Trap: Rs. 150 is the longer-period VWAP and may seem like the natural floor, but the rule takes the higher of both VWAPs. The legacy "26-week average weekly high-low / 2-week" formulation is no longer the current rule. Cross-Exam Context: NISM IX and XV both test preferential-issue pricing using the current 90/10 trading-day VWAP rule.
